label: early copy step (outputting original token 2) in short sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L); never during the original tokens or on the <DEL> step, and never when the input token is appearing for the first time. Activity is concentrated on short sequences (L=3 copy steps are active ~21% of the time vs ~1% baseline; L=3-4 hold ~66% of mass) and on early recall positions (recall_idx 2 holds 56% of mass, recall_idx 1-4 hold ~98%). The strongest activations are at L=3, step 5: input orig(1), output orig(2) (e.g. c f t <DEL> c [f]); L=3 recall_idx 2 alone has precision ~0.79. Magnitude is also modulated by the identity of the fed-back input (t, f, p are highest; digits are low), which the predicate does not capture. A weaker tail fires at early-to-mid copy steps of long sequences (L=8-9, t=10-13), often when an earlier original token was a digit; this is not captured. Low precision for L=4 and token dependence make this only a partial explanation.
